t:
The Secretary is authorized to make payments on the following conditions with respect to sugar or liquid sugar commecially recoverable from the sugar beets or sugarcane grown on a farm for the extraction of sugar or liquid sugar:

    (a) 
That no child under the age of fourteen years shall have been employed or permitted to work on the farm, whether for gain to such child or any other person, in the production, cultivation, or harvesting of a crop of sugar beets or sugarcane with respect to which application for payment is made, except a member of the immediate family of a person who was the legal owner of not less than 40 per centum of the crop at the time such work was performed; and that no child between the ages of fourteen and sixteen years shall have been employed or permitted to do such work, whether for gain to such child or any other person, for a longer period than eight hours in any one day, except a member of the immediate family of a person who was the legal owner of not less than 40 per centum of the crop at the time such work was performed. The Secretary is authorized to make payments, notwitstanding a failure to comply with the conditions provided in this subsection but the payments made with respect to any crop shall be subject to a deduction of $10 for each child for each day, or a portion of a day, during which such child was employed or permitted to work contrary to the foregoing provisions of this subsection.
 
    (b) 
That there shall not have been marketed (or processed) an amount (in terms of planted acreage, weight, or recoverable sugar content) of sugar beets or sugarcane grown on the farm and used for the production of sugar or liquid sugar to be marketed in, or so as to compete with or otherwise directly affect interstate or foreign commerce, in excess of the proportionate share for the farm, as determined by the Secretary pursuant to the provisions of section 302, of the total quantity of sugar beets or sugarcane required to be processed to enable the area in which such sugar beets or sugarcane are produced to meet the quota (and provide a normal carry-over inventory) as estimated by the Secretary for such area for the calendar year during which the larger part of the sugar or liquid sugar from such crop normally would be marketed.
 
    (c) 

        (1) 

That all persons employed on the farm in the production, cultivation, or harvesting of sugar beets or sugarcane with respect to which an application for payment is made shall have been paid in full for all such work, and shall have been paid wages therefor at rates not less than those that may be determined by the Secretary to be fair and reasonable after investigation and due notice and opportunity for public hearing; and in making such determinations the Secretary shall take into consideration the standards therefor formerly established by him under the Agricultural Adjustment Act, as amended, and the differences in conditions among various producing areas: 
Provided, however, That a payment which would be payable except for the foregoing provisions of this subparagraph may be made, as the Secretary may determine, in such manner that the laborer will receive an amount, insofar as such payment will suffice, equal to the amount of the accrued unpaid wages for such work, and that the producer will receive the remainder, if any, of such payment.

 
        (2) 

That the producer on the farm who is also, directly or indirectly a processor of sugar beets or sugarcane, as may be determined by the Secretary shall have paid, or contracted to pay under either purchase or toll agreements, for any sugar beets or sugarcane grown by other producers and processed by him at rates not less than those that may be determined by the Secretary to be fair and reasonable after investigation and due notice and opportunity for public hearing.

fable.w: The Secretary must set fair and reasonable wage rates (and fair prices for sugar beets or sugarcane) only after investigation, due notice, and an opportunity for public hearing, which brings the general public into a federal determination. The tempting reading is that the section only sets conditions on benefit payments to producers, and applications for payments are not participation. That reading fails because the public hearing attaches to the Secretary's rate-setting decision, not to the payment application itself.
fable.s: shall have been paid wages therefor at rates not less than those that may be determined by the Secretary to be fair and reasonable after investigation and due notice and opportunity for public hearing

qwen_block.w: The section explicitly requires the Secretary to determine fair and reasonable wage rates after providing 'due notice and opportunity for public hearing.' A public hearing is a form of participation where the general public or interested parties can provide input before a federal decision is made. This fits the definition of participation involving the general public.
qwen_block.s: shall have been paid wages therefor at rates not less than those that may be determined by the Secretary to be fair and reasonable after investigation and due notice and opportunity for public hearing

opus.w: Before the Secretary sets the fair and reasonable wage rates and processor payment rates, the statute requires due notice and an opportunity for a public hearing. That lets the general public, growers, processors and laborers take part in a federal decision. The payment-application setting doesn't change this: the hearing applies to the Secretary's rate-setting, not to anyone applying for a benefit.
opus.s: shall have been paid wages therefor at rates not less than those that may be determined by the Secretary to be fair and reasonable after investigation and due notice and opportunity for public hearing
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** This could look like a "No" because the section is about the conditions for benefit payments, and applying for benefits doesn't count as participation. But that reading fails here. Before the Secretary decides what wage rates and sugar beet/sugarcane purchase prices are "fair and reasonable," the section requires "due notice and opportunity for public hearing." A public hearing before a federal decision brings outsiders into that decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary to determine fair and reasonable wage rates after providing 'due notice and opportunity for public hearing.' A public hearing is explicitly listed in the definition as a form of participation where the general public can consult or coordinate with the government before a decision is made. Although the context involves payments to farmers (which are generally excluded as applications for benefits), the specific mechanism of a public hearing for setting wage standards involves outside parties (the public) in a federal decision, thus meeting the criteria for participation.
qwen_chat.s: That all persons employed on the farm in the production, cultivation, or harvesting of sugar beets or sugarcane with respect to which an application for payment is made shall have been paid in full for all such work, and shall have been paid wages therefor at rates not less than those that may be determined by the Secretary to be fair and reasonable after investigation and due notice and opportunity for public hearing
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "public hearing" mentioned in subsection (c) is merely a procedural step for the Secretary to determine fair wages, and since the primary context is payments to farmers (which are excluded as "applications for benefits"), the section does not involve participation. However, the definition explicitly states that a "public hearing" before a federal decision is a form of participation, regardless of the underlying benefit program. The key is that the general public is invited to participate in the decision-making process (setting wage rates) via a hearing.
